transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Liu (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (NorthStar AM), Rajiv Menon (NorthStar SE), Maya Chen (NorthStar Channel Head)

00:00 Jamie (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, hopin' we can run through the partner pipeline and focus on the Meridian opportunity today
00:08 Lena (NorthStar AM): yeah thanks jamie, we got a few folks on from northstar, hope that's okay, quick agenda was pipeline updates, any blockers, and co-sell asks
00:18 Samir (Redwood SE): hi all, i'll jump in on the technical asks, latency, cost numbers, and quick plan for the benchmark. there's a shared sheet, i think jamie sent it? link: https://redwood.app/spreadsheets/pipeline-northstar
00:30 Maya (Channel Head): perfect, um Meridian is top priority, they want production timeline Q3 and security review early april
00:38 Jamie: ok great, let's start with Meridian. lena, can you summarize current stage and what they need from us to close?
00:46 Lena: Meridian's at an exec favor stage, they like the product, but procurement is slow. they asked for dedicated deployment options and a timeline for SOC2 docs and KMS support. they also want cost estimates versus their current vendor, which is MegaCloud
01:02 Jamie: got it. samir, can you confirm dedicated capacity guarantees and typical latency for the retail workload?
01:10 Samir: yeah, for dedicated we can guarantee throughput tiers with SLA. typical p99 latencies we've seen for similar seq lengths are around 220-280ms on A100 equivalent nodes; with batching tuned it can drop to ~150ms for requests under 1k tokens but depends on prompt complexity. also quantized variants further reduce cost but add a small quality delta
01:36 Rajiv (NorthStar SE): that latency sounds okay, but meridian is concerned about peak shopping events, like black friday. they need autoscale and burst capacity metrics
01:47 Samir: we can show historic scaling patterns; our autoscale adds burst nodes within ~90s with warm pools, and burst to cold starts takes longer. we should run a sim to show behavior under a traffic spike
01:59 Jamie: action there: samir to prepare benchmark plan and scripts to simulate peak traffic for meridian. due next tuesday?
02:07 Samir: yes i'll target 2026-04-07, that gives time to validate both dedicated and hosted configurations
02:15 Lena: procurement is asking for a KMS/HSM integration doc and audit logs. do you have references?
02:23 Jamie: yes we have a security pack, i'll drop the SOC2 and KMS guide in the shared folder. note: some names in the doc are a bit messy, apologies, the auto-export sometimes mangles acronyms (K M S spelled KMS in doc tho)
02:38 Maya: also need SSO + SAML details for their security team
02:43 Samir: we support SAML and SCIM, and we can push logs to customer's SIEM. we'll include an architecture slide showing VPC peering and private deployment options
02:57 Lena: great. next on pipeline: there's a lead called VertexCorp — procurement is the big blocker. we need an intro.
03:05 Jamie: who owns the contact?
03:07 Lena: unknown on our side, but i can try to intro. northstar has an existing business relationship, should be quick
03:12 Jamie: ok next step: lena to provide intro to procurement/legal contact at vertexcorp by 2026-04-05
03:20 Rajiv: any concerns about data residency? VertexCorp wants eu data at-rest within EU region
03:27 Samir: we can provision region-specific deployments, private control plane available for enterprise, and we have KMS options in EU regions. will note potential latency differences for cross-region routing though
03:41 Jamie: competitors — meridian ran a proof with MegaCloud and also looked at TitanAI for embedding-heavy workloads. we should highlight where we win: cost at scale, better caching, and predictable latency with dedicated pools
03:57 Samir: technically our prefix/KV caching and continuous batching give lower token costs for repeat conversational flows. we'll include cost-per-1M-token comparatives in the spreadsheet but mark the assumptions (seq length, cache hit rate)
04:14 Lena: can you send that spreadsheet after the call? i want northstar's commercial team to review
04:18 Jamie: yes will update and share. i'll also add an ask column per opportunity (e.g., joint exec call, benchmark, security docs)
04:26 Maya: for meridian execs, they want a short 30 minute demo focused on latency, stability, and integration path. can we do that next week?
04:33 Jamie: yes let's target next thursday 10am PT, i'll send a calendar hold
04:38 Samir: for the demo, i'll prepare a live demo on dedicated pool and a quick comparison of hosted vs dedicated for latency/cost. want me to include a simulated Black Friday spike?
04:49 Maya: yes please, that's the top ask
04:52 Rajiv: one more technical note — meridian uses an internal ranking model, they'd like to run a reranking flow that calls both redwood and their model. is function calling supported?
05:01 Samir: we have tool-calling and structured output; we can show an example of a rerank pipeline and how to keep tokens low using KV cache. but need to validate compatibility with their model container if they want on-prem integration
05:17 Lena: ok good. any other deals on the sheet we should call out?
05:21 Jamie: yes there's Meridian (high priority, ARR 1.2M), VertexCorp (mid, 420k opportunity), and a smaller retail pilot Meridian-us-east (pilot 75k) — i'll add ARR estimates into the sheet
05:36 Maya: are we tracking win-probabilities? northstar uses a forecast column, could you align on that?
05:42 Jamie: good point, we'll align on stage-to-probability mapping in the sheet, i'll propose numbers and we can sync next week
05:49 Rajiv: procurement sometimes asks for a runbook on incident response, do you have a template?
05:55 Samir: yes we have an incident response runbook and SLA details, i'll include that in the security pack
06:03 Lena: procurement will also ask for standard contract redlines; i'll flag the legal team to review once we have the main T&Cs
06:10 Jamie: ok, recap & next steps: 1) Redwood to update pipeline sheet with deals, ARR, and ask list (owner: Jamie, due 2026-04-02). 2) Samir to prepare benchmark and test scripts for dedicated vs hosted (owner: Samir, due 2026-04-07). 3) Lena to intro to VertexCorp procurement (owner: Lena, due 2026-04-05). 4) Schedule joint demo for Meridian next Thursday 10am PT (owner: Jamie).
06:36 Maya: that sounds good, thanks everyone
06:40 Jamie: thanks all, i'll send notes and links right after, and we'll follow up in the sheet. end of call

Notes: transcription contains typical auto-transcription imperfections: names/acronyms sometimes hyphenated or mangled. references to docs: https://redwood.app/spreadsheets/pipeline-northstar and security pack link: https://redwood.app/docs/security-pack-northstar
